posts.mainText: Federal agencies tasked via executive order to review state AI laws conflicting with federal innovation priorities, advancing unified national AI governance.
posts.replyText: Bolsters federal-state institutional coordination, mitigating risks of regulatory patchwork undermining AI leadership and competitiveness.

posts.mainText: GSA's proposed AI clause demands contractors use only American AI systems, segregate government data, report incidents in 72 hours, and disclose full AI supply chains.
posts.replyText: Transforms federal procurement into a governance lever, mandating coordinated safety practices across government contractors for enhanced legitimacy.

posts.mainText: Senator Blackburn released draft TRUMP AMERICA AI Act March 18, imposing duty of care on AI developers, ending Section 230 immunity for harms, protecting minors.
posts.replyText: Seeks to establish authoritative federal AI regulation, coordinating institutional efforts and legitimizing oversight amid state-level fragmentation.

posts.mainText: New analysis on AI agents highlights cascading risks requiring coordinated action: holistic standards, observability, and international collaboration for system-level safety.
posts.replyText: Drives cross-organization AI safety initiatives, addressing legitimacy gaps in current model-focused governance unable to handle interconnected threats.

posts.mainText: Policymakers warned of 'evidence dilemma' in AI governance: delaying action for 'smoking gun' proof risks irreversible harm from rapid AI advances.
posts.replyText: Underscores need for proactive institutional coordination and legitimacy through anticipatory regulation, not just reactive evidence-based responses.
